toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The departures are concentrated in one place: 8 of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter resigned, against 1 of 13 who were never on it. All 11 Kestrel associates report to the same new partner, Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no one else. Pay is the same across the group, and the billable-target change applied to every group. Neither explains why only Kestrel staff are leaving. So I doubt the retention payment would fix the problem, and announcing it and closing the review would be a mistake.

What I can't tell is whether the cause is the workload (months of weekends on document review) or Faulk's supervision (late-night corrections copied to the whole team). On the records, the two can't be separated. Survey comments point to both. I only collected one piece of evidence, so my confidence on that point is low.

Next step: commission the confidential external interviews, about £9k and three weeks. Ask questions that separate supervision from workload. Then pick the fix, which may be contract reviewers, a change of supervisor, or both. Also start tracking matter and supervising partner in attrition reports.
